name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd

concall.name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd

takeaways.label: Volume and participation hit new baselines
takeaways.text: ADT nearly doubled YoY to ₹12.6 lakh crores, traded clients in H1 already reached 19.8 lakh against 20.9 lakh for all of FY26, and management sees a step-up in the structural baseline across segments.

takeaways.label: Scalability confirmed in the P&L
takeaways.text: H1 revenue from operations of ₹1,501 cr and PAT of ₹868 cr at a 75% EBITDA margin demonstrate the operating leverage in the model, even as the company invests ahead of growth.

takeaways.label: Regulatory tailwinds are material but incomplete
takeaways.text: SEBI's SGF rationalization cut the Z-score requirement from 10 to 5, pausing contributions for a few quarters, while the FPI circular for non-agri commodities is still awaited and could unlock a new participation layer.

takeaways.label: Product and delivery innovation is broadening the funnel
takeaways.text: Far-dated futures (up to 18 months for crude), consolidated delivery locations, and micro-options are all gaining traction, widening the addressable use-case set beyond short-tenor speculation.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the awaited FPI circular for gold and silver is formalized, the pace of electricity derivatives adoption beyond the current ₹77 cr ADT, and how the baseline sustains if volatility normalizes.

points.label: ADT nearly doubled YoY
points.text: to ₹12.6 lakh crores, with a 20% QoQ step-up, reflecting wider adoption of commodity derivatives for both hedging and investment.

points.label: Client count approaching full-year FY26 in six months
points.text: H1 traded clients hit 19.8 lakh, close to the FY26 full-year figure of 20.9 lakh, signaling faster awareness and acceptance.

points.label: Growth is broad, not concentrated
points.text: Participation increases span retail and proprietary segments, with proportional contributions unchanged even after the RBI bank guarantee circular took effect in July, though some credit squeeze was acknowledged.

points.label: FPI volumes are growing from a small base
points.text: Currently in late single-digit percentage contribution, FPIs are active in cash-settled crude oil and natural gas contracts, with heightened interest in India-specific contracts that have price discovery and delivery linkage to the domestic context.

points.label: Management does not want any single segment to dominate
points.text: The stated preference is for mature, well-aware participation across segments rather than a retail surge resembling equity F&O scale, which management says is neither expected nor the objective.

quotes.text: Praveena Rai: "I think we see a healthy improvement and healthy increase in the baseline when it comes to participation products and not just certain segments of participation, but participation across segments. And I think this gives us the confidence that there is a new baseline with every step of growth that our business is really seeing here now."

points.label: Far-dated futures now live
points.text: in aluminium, copper, zinc (up to 12 months) and crude oil (up to 18 months), extending the hedging horizon for physical market participants.

points.label: Delivery logistics simplified
points.text: Single and distinct delivery locations introduced for lead (Chennai) and zinc (Thane), with mini contracts for lead (Palwal) and zinc (Kolkata), effective November 2026, aimed at reducing the operational friction of multiple GST registrations.

points.label: Smaller contracts are gaining traction
points.text: Silver 100-gram futures crossed ₹100 cr ADT, Gold 10-Gram Futures launched last year remain popular, and silver micro-options at 30 kg, 5 kg and 1 kg are all in significant play.

points.label: Electricity derivatives show early depth
points.text: Q2 ADT of ~₹77 cr (vs H1 ADT of ₹57 cr) with open interest visible in the second and third month, not just the current month, indicating some value-chain participants are using the market; MCX holds ~75% market share.

points.label: More products are in the pipeline
points.text: but launches are being paced so the market can absorb them; announcements will come at the appropriate time.

points.label: SGF rationalization is a material cost tailwind
points.text: SEBI's August 2026 circular cut the Z-score requirement from 10 to 5, bringing the SGF contribution requirement down sharply; existing contributions are sufficient for 2–3 quarters, after which contributions resume at a far more optimized level.

points.label: No SGF provision was made in Q2
points.text: A similar quantum to Q1 would have been required otherwise, making this a direct P&L benefit for the quarter.

points.label: FPI access expansion is pending
points.text: A SEBI consultation paper proposes allowing FPIs in non-agri commodities (gold, silver), but the final circular has not been formalized; MCX is waiting and expects FPIs to play an increasing role once it arrives.

points.label: Physical delivery remains compulsory
points.text: for all non-agri physical delivery contracts, a structural feature that will apply to any new FPI participation framework.

points.label: Technology costs rose with capacity, not as one-time spend
points.text: The increase is driven by incremental running expenses from capacity nearly doubled in recent months; these are ongoing operating expenses, while one-time capacity build goes to capex.

points.label: Product license fees move with volume
points.text: The sharp increase in license fees is linked to turnover, mainly the crude pricing license from CME, and moves in proportion to volume increases.

points.label: Effective tax rate spiked in Q2 on a one-time catch-up
points.text: Subsidiary MCXCCL made a tax provision and the annual effective rate was re-evaluated based on a SEBI circular, with the YTD impact booked entirely in Q2; the rate is expected to normalize closer to 25% going forward.

points.label: EBITDA margin sustainability is a deliberate choice to invest
points.text: Management will continue to invest in scale, technology changes, information security, and innovation, but expects to do so smartly; baseline growth is expected to sustain quarter-on-quarter, and EBITDA will be the result of those actions, not a target to defend in isolation.

quotes.text: Praveena Rai: "I don't think we really want to put a number or a projection around the EBITDA margins."

points.label: Management is taking competition seriously
points.text: but notes that not much headway has been made by competitors so far; MCX intends to do whatever is required to remain competitive and hold its space.

points.label: No market share prediction offered
points.text: When asked where share could settle in 3–5 years, management declined to forecast, saying only that it will do what is needed to be very competitive.

points.label: Metal segment has headroom but structural limits
points.text: Copper is demonstrating growth and momentum, but the metal segment is not expected to reach the levels of precious metals.

points.label: Premium-to-notional ratio in options
points.text: is not expected to inch up immediately; it depends on volatility, contract types, and duration as the market matures.

quotes.text: Praveena Rai: "You tell me. We can't make any prediction like that. I think we are certainly taking competition seriously. And not much headway has been made till now in terms of the competition for us to lose share."

points.label: Volatility management is the top operational priority
points.text: The team focuses on ensuring market integrity, surveillance, margins, settlements, and trade fructification during volatile periods, because that trust is the commitment to the market.

points.label: Cybersecurity is the second critical risk
points.text: MCX is working on multiple fronts, including using AI to protect against AI attacks, and collaborates closely with central organizations given its designation as national critical infrastructure.

points.label: Technology capacity has been scaled proactively
points.text: Capacity nearly doubled in recent months, supporting higher per-day peaks seamlessly, and the exchange will continue to invest efficiently as long as growth is expected.

points.label: Data center operational expansion
points.text: is under review after stakeholder inputs; once the optimum approach is determined, it will be communicated.

quotes.text: Praveena Rai: "What really keeps our team up is to make sure that when markets are volatile, our surveillance is on track, our sort of making sure that there's no way that the market integrity suffers in any way because that's really the trust we commit to the market."

catalysts.name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd

items.title: Retail-sized bullion contracts
items.text: Gold Ten (10g) futures launched April 2025 hit ₹453 crore ADT in FY26, and Silver 100 (100g) futures launched June 2026 already run about ₹100 crore ADT; monthly silver options ADT grew 606% to ₹43,899 crore after June 2025 expiries. Small-lot products open commodity trading to retail investors - only 35% of equity traders currently trade commodities - and bullion already contributes 69% of ADT.

items.title: Electricity futures ramp-up
items.text: India's first power derivative launched July 2025 with an IEX price-reference agreement; ADT doubled from ₹37 crore in Q1 FY27 to ₹77 crore in Q2 FY27 with market share around 75% and about 50 commercial participants onboarded. India's spot power market is the world's third largest, and derivatives turnover is currently only ~70 bps of deliverable supply versus far higher multiples in Europe, China and America.

items.title: Coal exchange subsidiary
items.text: MCX won the Coal Exchange license (SEBI approval April 17, 2026), incorporated MCX Coal Exchange of India in June 2026 with up to ₹100 crore capital, and launched coal and minerals trading platforms in October 2026. A pan-India spot coal market adds a new revenue line outside derivatives and lays the foundation for covering the whole energy basket.

items.title: Mineral exchange subsidiary
items.text: SEBI approved the mineral spot exchange investment on August 11, 2026, and the wholly owned subsidiary MCX Mineral Exchange of India was incorporated October 16, 2026, with a license application to the Indian Bureau of Mines to follow. It extends the exchange franchise into physical trading of mined resources, a second new spot platform within six months.

items.title: FPI and institutional access
items.text: About 250 FPIs are onboarded as of Q2 FY27, contributing 2-3% of ADT but a double-digit share within energy, and a SEBI consultation is in process to extend FPI access beyond cash-settated contracts to gold and silver. Banks as Professional Clearing Members, mutual funds via hybrid schemes and Portfolio Managers are now permitted, widening the institutional base.

items.title: Base metals contract deepening
items.text: Copper futures ADT grew 86% to ₹3,559 crore and copper options ADT 1,234% to ₹2,536 crore in FY26 after single delivery-center and warehouse rationalization changes; nickel relaunched August 2025 with smaller lots for MSMEs. From November 2026, lead and zinc delivery consolidates to single locations, easing GST registration for hedgers and incentivizing exchange use.

items.title: Commodity index products
items.text: Options on BULLDEX launched October 2025, and management is reworking both futures and options on the index while moving forward on METALDEX this year, with regulatory approvals already in hand for further new products. Indices give investors a diversified commodity entry point and deepen the options franchise beyond single contracts.

items.title: Far-dated energy futures
items.text: Futures now extend to 12 months in aluminium, copper and zinc and 18 months in crude oil, added on corporate and institutional demand. Longer tenors support the energy segment's Q2 FY27 futures-plus-options ADT of ₹3,97,820 crore, up 127% YoY.
